blindSummary:
This state/province replicates the border-checkpoint script of an adjoining state/province: border-district police arrested a transgender national of the neighbouring country for allegedly "infiltrating" the country, treating trans appearance as evidence of illegal entry rather than identity; officers also detained the e-rickshaw driver who had carried her across the border. The state/province shares a long border with the neighbouring country and falls within the same policing logic. It is also one of only three states/provinces recording cases under the national transgender law in 2021 (3 of 7 nationwide), indicating some legal infrastructure exists but also that trans-targeted crime is occurring at a detectable rate.

The border profiling is visitor-facing and security-force-driven, though the incidents are fewer and less concentrated than the repeated sweep operations documented next door. A welfare board exists (one of 12 constituted bodies nationwide) but per a right-to-information investigation it operates without a functioning policy framework. For a foreign visitor transiting the land border, the primary exposure is the same appearance-as-suspicion-trigger mechanism documented in the adjoining state/province; outside the region's largest city there is little offsetting civic infrastructure.

The government's official press portal (8 Dec 2021, the ministry in charge): state-wise list of the 12 states/provinces and centrally administered territories that had constituted transgender welfare boards under the national transgender rules — this state/province included. Official record of the board's existence.

Right-to-information investigation by a national news outlet (5 Nov 2024) into state transgender welfare boards: most constituted boards lack leadership or real power — the basis for treating this state/province's board as nominal.
blindOutOfScope: General cross-border crime and immigration enforcement in the border belt affects all populations; only the trans-appearance-as-infiltration-evidence framing is state-policy relevant to trans travellers.
